```

The code below runs in a new R session with MIRA installed. The small
helper reads the metric-name map preserved on MIRA tables; keep its definition
when copying the later extraction examples.

```{r reader-tools}
library(MIRA)
metric_columns <- function(table, bases) {
  mapping <- attr(table, "mira_metric_names")
  actual <- bases
  mapped <- bases %in% names(mapping)
  actual[mapped] <- unname(mapping[bases[mapped]])
  stopifnot(all(actual %in% names(table)))
  actual
}
```

## Three measurements answer different ophthalmic questions

This article assumes the single-outcome and
[missing-data](frequentist-long-missing-data.html) tutorials. The new task is
to retain separate units, schedules and extraction states for several measures
from the same prespecified study eye, rather than fit a joint multivariate model.

A synthetic retinal-edema follow-up study measures BCVA in ETDRS letters,
OCT central-subfield thickness and IOP. More correctly read letters represent
better measured acuity. Here `cmt` means the mean retinal thickness in the
central 1-mm-diameter subfield in micrometres (um), not a central-point thickness.
The [DRCR Retina Network](https://public.jaeb.org/drcrnet/stdy/149)
documents the separate use of visual-acuity and OCT central-subfield measures.
The simulated OCT protocol is the same at every visit; cross-device conversion
is not attempted. Anatomical thinning is not automatically functional improvement; the
[DRCR study of OCT and visual acuity](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17123615/)
also treats thickness and vision as distinct measurements.

IOP is a safety measurement in mmHg in this retinal cohort. We deliberately
leave its favorable direction **unknown**: this is not an elevated-pressure
treatment question, and neither an increase nor a decrease alone establishes
net clinical benefit. Pooling letters, micrometres and mmHg would be meaningless.

Each of the 72 adults contributes one study eye whose laterality is assigned
before generating measurements. The fellow eye is absent, so one row and ID
represent one independent participant and their selected eye. Shared retinal
severity makes higher thickness and lower acuity tend to occur together,
while independent measurement errors keep the relationship imperfect. IOP
has its own person component. These are assumed synthetic distributions,
not estimates from a clinical trial or validated disease-measurement models.

```{r multi-outcome-data}
set.seed(443041)
n <- 72L
study_eye <- sample(c("Right", "Left"), n, replace = TRUE)
retinal_severity <- rnorm(n)
acuity_person <- -7 * retinal_severity + rnorm(n, 0, 4)
thickness_person <- 45 * retinal_severity + rnorm(n, 0, 25)
pressure_person <- rnorm(n, 0, 1.8)
retina <- data.frame(
  participant_id = sprintf("R%03d", seq_len(n)), study_eye = study_eye,
  bcva_t0 = round(56 + acuity_person + rnorm(n, 0, 3)),
  bcva_t3 = round(60 + acuity_person + rnorm(n, 0, 4)),
  bcva_t6 = round(64 + acuity_person + rnorm(n, 0, 4)),
  cmt_t0 = 435 + thickness_person + rnorm(n, 0, 22),
  cmt_t6 = 380 + thickness_person + rnorm(n, 0, 27),
  cmt_t12 = 350 + thickness_person + rnorm(n, 0, 30),
  iop_t0 = 16.5 + pressure_person + rnorm(n, 0, 1.0),
  iop_t6 = 17.0 + pressure_person + rnorm(n, 0, 1.2)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(retina$participant_id), !anyNA(retina$participant_id),
  all(as.matrix(retina[grep("^bcva_", names(retina))]) >= 0),
  all(as.matrix(retina[grep("^(cmt|iop)_", names(retina))]) > 0))
retina$bcva_t6[c(5, 11, 24, 43, 68)] <- NA_real_
retina$cmt_t6[c(8, 16, 24, 59)] <- NA_real_
retina$cmt_t12[c(8, 16, 32, 59, 65)] <- NA_real_
retina$iop_t6[c(2, 24, 39, 58)] <- NA_real_
str(retina)
```

## Inspect automatic detection before analysis

The built-in `"auto"` parser recognizes these `_t<number>` suffixes and
groups columns by outcome family. Inspection resolves the configuration
without fitting models or computing outcome summaries. Names alone do not
establish what an outcome measures or whether increasing values are favorable.

```{r automatic-outcomes}
detected <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "auto",
  covariates = character(0), variable_pattern = "auto",
  analyses = "none", inspect_only = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
detected$config$outcomes
detected$config$time_vars
detected$config$improvement_direction
stopifnot(setequal(detected$config$outcomes, c("bcva", "cmt", "iop")))
auto_fit <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "participant_id", covariates = character(0),
  analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
class(auto_fit)
names(auto_fit$outcomes)
```

The inspection output maps BCVA to higher and both CMT and IOP to lower.
These are name-based defaults, not a clinical assessment. `auto_fit` above
demonstrates naming/provenance only; it is not the prespecified IOP safety
analysis. The explicit configuration below overrides IOP to `"unknown"` before
any safety classification is interpreted.

An automatically inferred outcome name does not prefix metric columns.
Explicitly declaring an outcome name through `outcomes` or a named
`time_vars` element does prefix its metrics. Both forms carry the
`mira_metric_names` attribute, which maps canonical metrics to actual
columns. A display label is not the metric prefix. Preserve this provenance
when constructing extraction code.

## Specify schedules and interpretations per outcome

The next call makes the scientific mapping explicit. Different numbers of
visits are allowed for different outcomes; each must have at least two
numeric measurement columns. The names in all per-outcome settings must
match the selected outcome names uniquely after MIRA's case-and-punctuation
normalization. The actual strings below match exactly for readability.

```{r explicit-outcomes}
directions <- c(bcva = "higher", cmt = "lower", iop = "unknown")
thresholds <- c(bcva = 5, cmt = 25, iop = 1)
measurements <- list(
  bcva = c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t3", "bcva_t6"),
  "cmt" = c("cmt_t0", "cmt_t6", "cmt_t12"),
  iop = c("iop_t0", "iop_t6")
)
visit_labels <- list(
  bcva = c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6"),
  "cmt" = c("Baseline", "Month 6", "Month 12"),
  iop = c("Baseline", "Month 6")
)
multi_fit <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "participant_id", outcomes = names(measurements),
  time_vars = measurements, time_labels = visit_labels,
  improvement_direction = directions, stable_threshold = thresholds,
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none",
  alpha = 0.05, p_adjust_method = "holm", verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(inherits(multi_fit, "mira_info_multi_long"),
          identical(names(multi_fit$outcomes), names(measurements)),
          !length(multi_fit$diagnostics$failed_outcomes))
multi_fit$config$improvement_direction
multi_fit$config$stable_threshold
```

MIRA analyzes the outcomes separately. This is not a multivariate joint
model, and correlation between outcomes is not modeled by the container.
All outcomes share the call's `alpha`, `p_adjust_method`, covariates, and
optional-module selection. `improvement_direction`, `stable_threshold`,
`time_vars`, and `time_labels` can vary by outcome as shown. Use separate
public calls when outcomes require different covariates or analysis-module
settings; do not invent a per-outcome `analyses` argument.

## Navigate the result safely

A multi-outcome object has classes `mira_info_multi_long`, `mira_info_long`,
and `list`. Unlike a single-outcome result, its outcome-specific tables are
under `outcomes[[name]]`; there is no shared top-level `descriptives` table.
Each successful element is a complete `mira_info_long` result. Check the
multi-outcome class first when writing dispatch code, because the container
also inherits the single-outcome class.

```{r individual-result}
bcva_fit <- multi_fit$outcomes[["bcva"]]
class(bcva_fit)
bcva_fit$settings[c("improvement_direction", "stable_threshold")]
bcva_desc <- bcva_fit$descriptives
knitr::kable(bcva_desc[, metric_columns(bcva_desc, c(
  "label", "n", "mean", "sd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper"
))], digits = 2, col.names = c("Visit", "n", "Mean", "SD", "Lower", "Upper"),
caption = "BCVA (ETDRS letters) among study eyes observed at each visit; intervals concern the mean.")
attr(bcva_desc, "mira_metric_names")[c("mean", "sd")]
```

Global configuration validation errors stop the call. Unexpected analysis
errors are isolated per outcome in a multi-outcome call: an unsuccessful
element has class `mira_info_error_long` and fields `outcome` and `error`.
The container's `diagnostics$failed_outcomes` lists those names. A successful
container with a skipped module is different; inspect that module's
`performed`, `reason_skipped`, `warnings`, and `error` fields.

The following extractor handles both situations without hiding errors or
silently dropping unsuccessful outcomes. It returns a consistent summary
in canonical column names, while looking up the original metrics by their
mapping attribute.

```{r cross-outcome-extraction}
endpoint_summary <- function(result, outcome = NULL) {
  if (inherits(result, "mira_info_multi_long")) {
    if (is.null(outcome) || length(outcome) != 1L ||
        !outcome %in% names(result$outcomes)) {
      stop("Choose one named outcome from a multi-outcome result.")
    }
    return(endpoint_summary(result$outcomes[[outcome]]))
  }
  if (inherits(result, "mira_info_error_long")) {
    return(data.frame(outcome = result$outcome, status = result$error,
                      from = NA_character_, to = NA_character_, n = NA_integer_,
                      mean_change = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  }
  if (!inherits(result, "mira_info_long")) stop("Expected a MIRA analysis result.")
  if (is.null(result$change) || !is.data.frame(result$change)) {
    return(data.frame(outcome = result$outcome, status = "Change table absent",
      from = NA_character_, to = NA_character_, n = NA_integer_,
      mean_change = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  }
  change <- result$change
  row <- change$from == result$time_vars[[1L]] &
    change$to == result$time_vars[[length(result$time_vars)]]
  selected <- change[row, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(selected) == 0L) {
    endpoints <- result$time_vars[c(1L, length(result$time_vars))]
    return(data.frame(outcome = result$outcome,
      status = "No observed baseline-final pairs",
      from = unname(result$time_labels[endpoints[[1L]]]),
      to = unname(result$time_labels[endpoints[[2L]]]), n = 0L,
      mean_change = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  }
  stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1L)
  data.frame(
    outcome = result$outcome,
    status = if (selected$n == 1L) "One pair; interval unavailable" else
      if (all(is.finite(unlist(selected[, metric_columns(selected,
        c("mean_change", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")), drop = FALSE])))) "available" else
          "Mean or interval not estimable",
    from = selected$from_label, to = selected$to_label, n = selected$n,
    mean_change = selected[[metric_columns(selected, "mean_change")]],
    lower = selected[[metric_columns(selected, "ci_lower")]],
    upper = selected[[metric_columns(selected, "ci_upper")]]
  )
}
endpoint_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(multi_fit$outcomes, endpoint_summary))
rownames(endpoint_table) <- NULL
endpoint_units <- c(bcva = "ETDRS letters", cmt = "um", iop = "mmHg")
endpoint_table$unit <- unname(endpoint_units[endpoint_table$outcome])
knitr::kable(endpoint_table, digits = 2,
             caption = "Ophthalmic endpoint changes: retain each row's unit and follow-up duration; intervals are pointwise 95%.")
for (outcome in names(measurements)) {
  variables <- measurements[[outcome]]
  from <- retina[[variables[[1L]]]]
  to <- retina[[variables[[length(variables)]]]]
  paired <- is.finite(from) & is.finite(to)
  row <- endpoint_table[endpoint_table$outcome == outcome, , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1L, row$n == sum(paired),
            isTRUE(all.equal(row$mean_change, mean(to[paired] - from[paired]))))
}
multi_fit$diagnostics$failed_outcomes
lapply(multi_fit$outcomes, function(result) {
  if (inherits(result, "mira_info_error_long")) return(result$error)
  result$diagnostics$adaptation
})
```

The confidence intervals describe separate raw-scale mean changes in the
pairwise-observed samples. A letter, a micrometre and a mmHg are different units. BCVA change covers six months; OCT thickness
change covers twelve months. Comparing the numbers as if they were
commensurate effect sizes or identical follow-up estimands is inappropriate.
`summary(multi_fit)` supplies outcome-specific summaries and retains failed
elements, but selective extraction is preferable for manuscript tables.

A successful result can also contain no baseline-to-final pair: that is
an unavailable endpoint, rather than an outcome-level calculation error.
The extractor keeps that outcome visible with `n = 0` and missing estimates.
For one observed pair it retains the change but does not imply that its
uncertainty can be estimated. This separate copy removes the OCT thickness
endpoint deliberately; the main retina dataset and results are preserved.

```{r unavailable-endpoint}
no_endpoint_data <- retina
no_endpoint_data$cmt_t12 <- NA_real_
no_endpoint_fit <- mira_info_long(
  no_endpoint_data, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "cmt",
  time_vars = measurements[["cmt"]], time_labels = visit_labels[["cmt"]],
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
unavailable <- endpoint_summary(no_endpoint_fit)
stopifnot(inherits(no_endpoint_fit, "mira_info_long"), unavailable$n == 0L,
          is.na(unavailable$mean_change),
          identical(unavailable$status, "No observed baseline-final pairs"))
knitr::kable(unavailable,
             caption = "Unavailable OCT thickness endpoint retained without inventing an estimate (um).")
```

The one-pair state is also a real public-API output. Keep the first
participant's final measurement and mask all other final values on another
copy. We know a change for one person, but cannot estimate its sampling
standard deviation or a Student t interval from one difference.

```{r one-pair-endpoint}
one_pair_data <- retina
one_pair_data$cmt_t12[-1L] <- NA_real_
one_pair_fit <- mira_info_long(
  one_pair_data, id = "participant_id", outcomes = "cmt",
  time_vars = measurements[["cmt"]], time_labels = visit_labels[["cmt"]],
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
one_pair <- endpoint_summary(one_pair_fit)
stopifnot(one_pair$n == 1L, is.na(one_pair$lower), is.na(one_pair$upper),
  isTRUE(all.equal(one_pair$mean_change,
    retina$cmt_t12[1L] - retina$cmt_t0[1L])))
knitr::kable(one_pair, digits = 2,
  caption = "One observed OCT endpoint pair: change retained in um, uncertainty unavailable.")
selected_bcva <- endpoint_summary(multi_fit, outcome = "bcva")
stopifnot(identical(selected_bcva, endpoint_summary(bcva_fit)))
```

The extractor reports an absent change table separately from zero observed
endpoint pairs, and stops on a duplicated endpoint key. The ordinary examples
exercise available, zero-pair, one-pair, and multi-outcome dispatch states.
The absent-table and outcome-error branches are defensive contracts: a
deliberately constructed fixture or a software bug is not presented here as
an ordinary analytic result. Existing name-provenance, boundary, and public
API tests provide separate coverage of error isolation. The extractor's
`stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1L)` deliberately makes an unexpected duplicate
visible rather than arbitrarily selecting the first row.

## Response labels need a scientific threshold

For a threshold $c \geq 0$, MIRA labels a change greater than $c$ an
increase, a change below $-c$ a decrease, and a change in $[-c,c]$ stable.
The boundary is inclusive for stability. With `"lower"`, decreases become
`"Improved"`; with `"higher"`, increases do. `"unknown"` leaves clinical
direction missing while retaining numerical increase/decrease/stability.
These settings change labels and counts, not estimated means or tests.

The thresholds are 5 ETDRS letters, 25 um and 1 mmHg, chosen only to teach
unit-specific classification. They are not estimated by MIRA or validated
MCIDs, target-pressure rules or instrument-repeatability limits. For CMT,
"Improved" is only the software's name for a reduction exceeding the teaching
threshold; it does not establish visual improvement. IOP retains numerical
increase/decrease/stable labels but no favorable clinical label. Measurement
error, regression to the mean and missing endpoints affect these classifications.

```{r response-classification}
response_counts <- lapply(multi_fit$outcomes, function(result) {
  if (inherits(result, "mira_info_error_long")) return(result$error)
  table(result$trajectories$clinical_direction, useNA = "ifany")
})
response_counts
table(multi_fit$outcomes[["iop"]]$trajectories$direction, useNA = "ifany")
```

Missing endpoints and an unknown direction have different meanings even
though both can yield missing clinical labels. Use the numerical trajectory
metrics and settings to distinguish them. Automatic direction recognition
is intentionally limited: `bcva`, `visual_acuity`, and `va` map to higher;
`cmt`, `crt`, and `iop` map to lower; other names default to unknown.
Automatic thresholds default to zero. Neither is clinical validation. In this
retinal safety question, the automatic `iop -> lower` map is deliberately
overridden by `"unknown"`. Likewise, BCVA recorded on a logMAR scale would need
an explicit `"lower"` direction rather than the ETDRS-letter setting used here;
the function does not infer the acuity scale from the name `bcva`.

We can check response labels directly from the input endpoint differences,
including the participants with unavailable endpoints. A classification
describes an observed change; it is not an individual causal treatment
effect, and it does not incorporate measurement-error uncertainty.

```{r verify-response-labels}
for (outcome in names(measurements)) {
  variables <- measurements[[outcome]]
  delta <- retina[[variables[[length(variables)]]]] -
    retina[[variables[[1L]]]]
  expected <- ifelse(!is.finite(delta), NA_character_,
                     ifelse(delta > thresholds[[outcome]], "Increase",
                            ifelse(delta < -thresholds[[outcome]], "Decrease", "Stable")))
  trajectory <- multi_fit$outcomes[[outcome]]$trajectories
  input_order <- match(trajectory$patient, retina$participant_id)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(input_order),
            identical(trajectory$direction, expected[input_order]))
  if (directions[[outcome]] == "unknown") {
    stopifnot(all(is.na(trajectory$clinical_direction)))
  }
}
```

For comparison, a zero-threshold analysis calls every nonzero deviation a
numerical change. The mean-change estimates and paired p-values remain
identical. This check makes that distinction explicit.

```{r threshold-sensitivity}
zero_fit <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "participant_id", outcomes = names(measurements),
  time_vars = measurements, time_labels = visit_labels,
  improvement_direction = directions,
  stable_threshold = setNames(rep(0, length(measurements)), names(measurements)),
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "none", verbose = FALSE
)
for (outcome in names(measurements)) {
  original <- multi_fit$outcomes[[outcome]]$change
  zero <- zero_fit$outcomes[[outcome]]$change
  for (metric in c("mean_change", "paired_t_p", "paired_t_p_adj")) {
    stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
      original[[metric_columns(original, metric)]],
      zero[[metric_columns(zero, metric)]])))
  }
}
data.frame(
  outcome = names(measurements),
  stable_with_threshold = vapply(multi_fit$outcomes, function(x)
    sum(x$trajectories$direction == "Stable", na.rm = TRUE), integer(1L)),
  stable_with_zero = vapply(zero_fit$outcomes, function(x)
    sum(x$trajectories$direction == "Stable", na.rm = TRUE), integer(1L))
)
```

## Multiplicity across outcomes remains a study-level decision

The call's primary correction is applied within each outcome's implemented
comparison families. It does not control family-wise error or false
discovery rate across all outcomes, visits, methods, and subgroup analyses
in a research program. Correlated outcomes do not eliminate multiplicity.
Specify primary outcomes, estimands, and families before inspecting results;
coordinate any broader correction with that scientific plan. The stored raw
p-values allow a justified external study-level analysis, but selecting
favorable results after seeing them remains a problem.

## Select the outcome when plotting

For graphical exploration, include `"plots"` alongside the desired modules.
The multi-outcome plot method requires an outcome when more than one
succeeds. The following lightweight rerun stores plots for the three
outcomes and displays the BCVA trajectory. The figure summarizes the
participants observed at each visit and does not adjust for missingness.

```{r multi-outcome-plot, fig.cap="Observed BCVA means (ETDRS letters; higher denotes better measured acuity) with pointwise 95% Student-t mean intervals for one study eye per participant. Each visit uses its observed eyes; connecting means does not estimate paired change or impute missing acuity. The retinal cohort is synthetic."}
plot_fit <- mira_info_long(
  retina, id = "participant_id", outcomes = names(measurements),
  time_vars = measurements, time_labels = visit_labels,
  improvement_direction = directions, stable_threshold = thresholds,
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "plots", verbose = FALSE
)
if ("mean_ci" %in% names(plot_fit$outcomes[["bcva"]]$plots)) {
  display_fit <- plot_fit
  display_fit$outcomes[["bcva"]]$plots$mean_ci <-
    display_fit$outcomes[["bcva"]]$plots$mean_ci +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Scheduled visit", y = "BCVA (ETDRS letters)")
  plot(display_fit, outcome = "bcva", which = "mean_ci")
} else {
  plot_fit$outcomes[["bcva"]]$plot_error
}
```

See [descriptive analysis](frequentist-long-descriptive-analysis.html) for
individual trajectories and distribution plots. The
[reporting tutorial](frequentist-long-reporting.html) generates an auditable
multi-outcome bundle and locates each outcome's exported results.
